## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p3` · `domain:ui` · `area:records` · `pm:queue`. Option 1: the `simple` arm draws a self-contained inline entry, as every other arm does

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-04T13:55Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

**Why option 1, not "document the intersection".**
- One section contract across form types. objectstack-ai/objectstack#21704 fork 3 (ruled B) admits the inline arm on the page block without naming a form type. Five of six arms draw it. A `simple`-only exception would be a second contract that objectstack's section shape would have to carry.
- objectui#9884's pool intersection catches a **name-only** entry the object does not declare (a typo, or a stale name). An inline entry that carries its own `type` declares itself, so skipping it guards nothing.

**Direction:**
- `buildSectionFields`'s pooled branch (`sectionFields.ts` about `:480`–`:484`) draws an entry that carries its own `type`, the same way the pool-less branch does.
- Name-only entries keep the intersection and its warning.
- `ObjectFormSection.fields`' type (`packages/types/src/objectql.ts` about `:1497`) gains the form view's `{ field }` arm, which `sectionFields.ts` already draws.
- objectui's inline-sections test (`submitTargetRefusal.test.tsx`) adds the `simple` arm, so all six are run.

**Why p3.** The inline arm's measured writers (#21704's census: 7) are all in `plugin-form`'s README wizard and its tests, on the wizard arm, not on `simple`. Nothing drawn today goes missing. It closes a divergence before a writer reaches it.

**Routing:** `plugin-form`, so `domain:ui`. The type line rides the same PR.

**Serial:** objectui#11610 (`packages/types` form keys) and objectui#8347 (in flight on `packages/types/src/**`). The claim reads their file lists.

The in-flight objectui#11613 declares `packages/plugin-detail` and one console test.

## ACCEPT (content): PR objectui#11622, head `a49b506`. The contract review is still owed before landing

`domain:ui` execution seat 1 @ objectui · `session_015W8GBu6sBiqus2L2xjMsAL` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-04T17:58Z. Reviewed against GitHub and `origin/main`, not against the report.

**Checklist**
- **Shape:** draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #11615`, `Clause-②: yes` at the start of its own line. The body has no other closing keyword.
- **Triage ruling `5980751840` (option 1):** all four direction items are implemented. The pooled branch draws a self-describing inline entry, and name-only entries keep the intersection and its warning. `ObjectFormSection.fields` gains the `{ field }` arm, by reference to the spec's `FormFieldInput`. `simple` runs through the inline-sections blocks.
- **Zone 2 corrected by measurement, accepted:**
  - item 4: the discriminator is the existing `isInlineFieldDef`, not "carries its own `type`", because the spec's inline arm makes `type` optional. One predicate now serves both "needs no adapter" and "needs no pool".
  - item 2: the submit-refusal seam I flagged. `SimpleObjectForm`'s carve-out now reads the shared `hasInlineFieldSource`. The diff shows why that is consistent rather than a widening into a blanket escape: the old comment kept `hasInlineFields` precisely because sections never drew inline entries on `simple`, and they now do. Limb (b) stays all-or-nothing, so one name-only entry still refuses. Ablation A3 shows the carve-out is load-bearing, and the BOUNDARY case stays green.
  - item 3: no maintainer ruling in objectui#9884 or #11550 forbids the draw.
- **File surface, amended by the seat** (the claim listed 5 paths; the PR has 19). Each addition is either forced or owed:
  - `submitTarget.ts` exports `isInlineFieldDef` to reuse the one predicate. It is not re-exported from the package entry.
  - The five layout configs (`Tabbed`/`Wizard`/`Split`/`Drawer`/`ModalForm.tsx`) change one type line each. `tsc` forced them once the section type named the ruled arm, and a cast would have hidden what those layouts draw.
  - `index.tsx`: the `object-master-detail-form` `fields` description, which this change made false.
  - `objectql.zod.ts`: a comment only.
  - `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`: the stale `ObjectFormSection` row is removed from `CLAIM_DEBT`, a ledger shrink that `check:spec-symbols` demanded.
  - `README.md` and `content/docs/plugins/plugin-form.mdx`: the docs move with the behaviour.
- **Changeset:** `@object-ui/plugin-form: minor`, `@object-ui/types: minor`, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Its "what stays refused" and "behaviour change for an existing schema" paragraphs were checked against `buildSectionFields`, the carve-out and `formWritePayload`, and they hold.
- **Docs prose (seat-checked):** the new `plugin-form.mdx` section's sentences hold against the diff. The three entry shapes and their resolution are stated correctly. The `simple` pool and the warning are stated correctly. The all-inline collector's `onSuccess` is stated correctly.
- **Governed:** objectui `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` answers NOT GOVERNED for all 19 paths.

**Clause-② gate:** the claim declared `yes`, so `needs:contract-review` is hung on the PR in this stroke. An isolated review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` judges this head next. ⛔ No queue entry until a conforming PASS names the head and every check on it is green.

**Out-of-scope findings → Acceptance notes, not filed.** Neither has a measured door.
- With an `objectName` and no adapter, the `object-form` element gate's `requiresDataSource` exempts only non-empty `customFields`. So an all-inline-sections form shows the no-data-source notice before reaching any layout. It is loud, and the same on all six arms.
- `formWritePayload` strips an inline entry's undeclared key from an adapter write. That is by design (`sanitizeFormData`).
